newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - HSBC keeps up Latin American drive.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - HSBC keeps up Latin American drive.

text.p: Banking giant HSBC Holdings on Friday announced the latest in a series of moves into Latin American banking with the purchase of Argentina's Roberts Group for between $600 million and $688 million.
HSBC already has holdings in Argentina through its Midland Bank arm but the move on privately-owned financial services group Roberts dramatically extends its presence in the country.

"This further investment represents a significant commitment to the country. The Roberts Group will complement Banco HSBC Bamerindus in Brazil and be a valuable addition to our other investments in Latin America," said John Bond, HSBC's chief executive.

While not big by HSBC's standards, the Roberts deal is the latest in a string of deals in Latin American -- a region the banking giant says represents the most important of its strategies around the world.
The Roberts deal brings to some $2.0 billion the amount spent by HSBC in the area this year alone.

"The most significant changes have been in Latin America, where the group has made new investments to complement those we had in Chile, Brazil and Argentina for some time," HSBC chairman Sir William Purves told shareholders at the group's annual meeting.
In March, HSBC took a 10 percent stake in Banco del Sur del Peru, Peru's seventh largest retail bank and agreed to take a 20 percent shareholding in Mexico's Grupo Financiero Serfin.
Banca Serfin, Serfin's main subsidiary, is Mexico's third largest bank. HSBC paid around $300 million for its stake.

HSBC also took over Brazil's Banco Bamerindus, the country's fourth largest private bank, renaming it Banco HSBC Bamerindus. Purves said HSBC's standing and capital strength had enabled it to move swiftly into one of the world's fastest-growing banking markets.

At the time of the Bamerindus deal, which cost HSBC around $945 million, analysts welcomed the move, recognising the economic and political strides made by the major Latin American countries enhanced the continent's appeal for investment.
The deal to buy Roberts is subject to regulatory approvals and due diligence. It is expected to be completed in July.

Roberts has interests ranging from corporate, retail and investment banking to insurance, pensions and health care. It owns 70.1 percent of Banco Roberts, with the remaining 29.9 percent already held by HSBC.

Enrique Ruete, who will continue as chief executive of the Roberts Group, said HSBC would bring a new international dimension to the group and give it advantages not available to other banks in Argentina.
Banking giant HSBC has 5,000 offices in 78 countries and assets totalling 237 billion pounds ($388.1 billion) at the end of last year.
